title: Member Appeals Program Decision Turnaround Standards
content:
Under the Member Appeals Program, each internal level decides a standard appeal within a set number of calendar days from filing, and that number depends on the member's Northbridge Appeals package. All periods run from the filing of the appeal, except where a standard below says otherwise.

## Standard (non-urgent) appeals: calendar days from filing, for each internal level

| Package | Pre-service appeal | Post-service appeal (the member has already paid) |
|---|---|---|
| Northbridge Appeals Level One Delegated | 15 | 30 |
| Northbridge Appeals Two-Level Delegated | 15 | 30 |
| Northbridge Appeals Single-Level with External Review | 30 | 60 |
| Northbridge Appeals Two-Level with External Review | 15 | 30 |
| Northbridge Appeals State-Regulated Insured | 30 | 60 |
| Northbridge Appeals Full Fiduciary Delegation | 15 | 30 |

## Standards common to all six packages

- **Urgent appeals.** An urgent appeal is decided within 72 hours from filing. That single period covers all internal levels together.
- **Information requested from the appellant.** When the reviewer asks for information, the appellant has 45 calendar days to send it, with the request date counted as day zero.
- **Extension.** A standard post-service appeal may take one extension of 15 calendar days when the appellant has been asked for missing information.
- **Unclear timing.** An appeal whose timing is unclear is handled as a pre-service appeal.
- **Urgency without attestation.** An appeal filed as urgent without the required attestation is handled as a standard appeal, and the acknowledgment tells the appellant so.

## Worked illustrations (hypothetical)

- Under Northbridge Appeals Single-Level with External Review, a standard pre-service appeal is decided within 30 calendar days of filing. The same appeal under Northbridge Appeals Two-Level with External Review is decided within 15 calendar days of filing, and that period applies at each internal level.
- A standard post-service appeal under Northbridge Appeals State-Regulated Insured is due within 60 calendar days. If the appellant is asked for missing information, the package allows one extension of 15 calendar days.
- A request for information dated 1 April gives the appellant until 16 May to respond, because 1 April is day zero and 16 May is day 45.
